QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_33

question.text: Under SEBI's Code of Conduct for Investment Managers, a Manager who commits to transactions on behalf of the Fund must:

answer.text: Share all deal details with competing AIFs
Document all relevant correspondence and understanding during a deal with counterparties as per the records of the AIF

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the Code of Conduct in Chapter 11.6, where the Manager has committed to transactions on behalf of the Fund, all relevant correspondence and understanding during a deal with counterparties must be documented as per the records of the AIF. The Trap: Destroying correspondence, sharing deal details with competing AIFs and relying on oral commitments all contradict this record-keeping requirement. Note: The documentation duty is triggered once the Manager commits to transactions on behalf of the Fund.
